observable_outcome: The M3 local closure is provable without a real Provider CLI and without a Google Cloud dependency: a fake-Provider journey carries a provider-neutral Work Packet from issue intake to an Increment Artifact through enrollment, session, claim, lease, heartbeat and renew, workspace, permit, checkpoint and result acceptance; a Runner crash is survivable so that a different Execution with a strictly greater fencing token resumes from the durable journal while the crashed Execution's late Result is rejected; a real SIGKILL against a real process group proves the journal's fsync durability and the supervisor's TERM-then-KILL of a whole process group; a scope-limited, revocable, fail-closed Secret Broker injects a generated credential fixture into one child Invocation only, and that value is provably absent from the journal, the Work Packet, the bounded diagnostic log, the canonical store and the process argv while provably present in the Invocation environment; and devbox run --pure -- make check is green at the committed checkpoint with .agents/v2/evidence/V2-016-runner.json registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Every one of the 11 tests currently in internal/runner and the 3 in internal/provider still exists under the same name and still passes: TestControlLoopFsyncsReceiptAndObservation, TestControlLoopImmediateStopUnknownObservation, TestJournalRecoveryAndIdempotentAppend, TestJournalRejectsCorruptCompleteLine, TestWorkspaceAndGuard, TestSyntheticAndFakeProvider, TestOrchestratorFakeJourney, TestEnrollmentChallengeSignatureAndReplay, TestEnrollmentRejectsTamperedChallenge, TestEnrollmentTokenIsConsumedOnFirstBegin, TestSupervisorCancelsProcessGroupTERMThenKILL. Do not rewrite, rename or re-prove any of them. The only permitted edits to existing tests are the two named in A4 and A9. State the before and after test count in the evidence summary; the measured pre-change counts are 11 and 3.

A2. internal/runner gains a provider-neutral Work Packet boundary with no change under internal/provider. runner.ProviderRequest no longer has a Prompt field; it carries provider.WorkPacket plus the operation id and workspace. A new ProviderClient composes a provider.Adapter with an InvocationRunner seam; FakeInvocationRunner records the provider.Invocation and returns fixture bytes; SupervisedInvocationRunner runs a real Invocation through ProcessSupervisor into the bounded log and is the seam V2-017 fills. Tests build with the real provider.CodexAdapter and parse with the real provider.CodexAdapter.Parse against a fixture generated in the test, so no CLI is started and no quota is consumed. Assert that a WorkPacket failing provider.WorkPacket.Validate is refused before any Invocation is built.

A3. The journal recovery key is the increment/target identity plus an operation kind, not the per-attempt request id, and the journey takes an explicit attempt number from which per-attempt canonical request ids are derived. Prove both halves: a second attempt finds the pre-crash journal record while obtaining a genuinely new canonical Execution, and the same attempt number replayed twice is still idempotent (one result_accepted event, one provider call).

A4. Journey 1, local segment, is one self-contained test function in internal/runner/journey_test.go with its own t.TempDir() fixtures, its own context deadline and no package-level mutable state: issue an enrollment, complete the challenge, verify the session, use the resulting runner id as the claim caller, capture, plan, prepare, claim, create the workspace, start, tick the lease keeper across more than one LeaseTTL, obtain the process permit, build the Work Packet, run the fake Invocation, parse the Result, checkpoint, obtain the result permit, accept, and assert the terminal Execution status, the recorded checkpoint and the Increment Artifact digest. The journey must not sleep, must not start a goroutine timer and must use an injected clock and injected id generator. TestOrchestratorFakeJourney's assertion that Calls[0].Prompt is empty is replaced by the structural claim that the field no longer exists and a validated Work Packet is carried instead; that is the only change permitted to that test.

A5. Journey 4, local segment, is a second self-contained test function covering both crash positions. Case A, crash before the provider result is journaled: the new Execution re-runs the provider exactly once. Case B, crash after the provider result is journaled: the new Execution does not call the provider at all and adopts the recovered checkpoint. In both cases assert a different Execution id, a strictly greater fencing token, and that the crashed Execution's AcceptResult submitted under its old lease, version and fencing token is rejected with a domain error and leaves the new Execution's canonical state unchanged. Per dp-v2-016 d14, do not assert that the crashed Execution becomes Lost: that requires a reconciler pass owned by V2-019.

A6. internal/runner/crash_test.go proves real-process durability with a real signal: the test re-executes its own binary as a child (os.Args[0] plus a helper environment variable), the child opens a real runner.Journal under a directory the parent supplies, appends and fsyncs one event, writes a marker file and blocks, the parent polls for the marker with a bounded deadline and t.Fatal on timeout, then SIGKILLs the child's process group and confirms it is reaped, then a fresh OpenJournal on the same directory replays the fsync'd event intact. No fixed sleep anywhere, no privilege, no namespace, no container. State in the work report why this is deterministic on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest and that the layer split follows dp-v2-016 d4: this test carries the durability claim, journey 4 carries the state-machine claim, and both use the same Journal type and on-disk layout.

A7. TestSupervisorCancelsProcessGroupTERMThenKILL is strengthened, not replaced: the child spawns a grandchild in the same new process group, the test asserts that the grandchild is actually gone after cancellation and that TERM was delivered before KILL, observed through files the children write and polled with a bounded deadline. Prove the assertion binds by temporarily removing the syscall.Kill of the negated pid and confirming the test then fails, then restore. Record the before and after in the evidence: the current test passes even with the process-group kill removed, because the context deadline alone makes Run return a non-nil error.

A8. A Secret Broker exists in internal/runner with the two-channel design of dp-v2-016 d7. Lease takes a scope (execution id, repository, provider, fencing token, expiry) and a credential name list, and fails closed on: an expiry at or before now, a domain.PermitCredential denial under an effective stop, a credential name outside the per-provider allowlist, a zero or mismatched fencing token, and a second use of an already-consumed or revoked grant. Each of those five refusals has its own assertion. The granted environment is merged into the child environment inside the supervisor only; the guarded base environment still goes through GuardEnvironment unchanged, so GuardEnvironment([]string{"API_TOKEN=abc"}, ...) is still rejected. Only the credential identifier is ever recorded anywhere.

A9. A bounded diagnostic log sink exists: per-execution 0600 file under the data root and not under the workspace, a hard byte cap and a hard line cap, an explicit truncation marker, and RedactLog applied to every write. Assert that writing twice the cap yields a file no larger than the cap plus the bounded marker, that a secret-shaped value on child output is written as [REDACTED], and, as the positive control, that a non-secret value of the same length survives byte for byte. TestWorkspaceAndGuard's existing RedactLog assertion stays as it is; the new assertions go in log_test.go.

A10. Credential non-leakage is verified statically. internal/runner/source_guard_test.go extends the V2-010 go/ast pattern to this package's non-test files: no credential-shaped field name exists on any type that is marshalled into a journal event, a Work Packet, a canonical application request or a log line. The scan must read the AST, not the file text, because internal/runner legitimately names a Secret Broker and a PermitCredential kind. The matcher itself is verified against known-positive and known-negative names and the test fails outright on a zero-file scan, so it cannot pass vacuously. Record the file count scanned.

A11. Credential non-leakage is verified at runtime with a generated fixture and a positive control. The test derives a secret-shaped credential value from crypto/rand inside the test, never a real credential and never a value read from the environment or from disk outside t.TempDir(), passes it through the broker into one Invocation, and then asserts the value's bytes appear in none of: the journal file on disk, the marshalled Work Packet, the bounded diagnostic log file, the canonical store's recorded events, the accepted Result, and every element of the process argv. The same test asserts the value does appear in the Invocation environment, which is the positive control proving the search is not vacuous. State in the work report that a search asserting absence without a matching presence assertion proves nothing.

A12. Workspace write confinement is asserted at the strength dp-v2-016 d12 allows and no stronger: Invocation.WorkingDirectory equals the symlink-resolved workspace path, no argv element resolves outside the workspace root, the environment is allowlisted, the per-execution workspace is not a symlink and is not group or world accessible, and a write landing outside the workspace tree is detected by the test. Do not add a namespace sandbox and do not describe the assertion as OS-enforced confinement; docs/operations/runner-local.md must say plainly that OS-level confinement is deferred to a privileged container or VM integration test.

A13. A runner-side lease keeper calls application Renew and application Heartbeat as two separate operations over an injected clock with explicit ticks, never a background timer, and journey 1 exercises it across more than one LeaseTTL so that a provider run outliving the TTL keeps its lease. Assert that renew and heartbeat are distinct calls with distinct request ids, that a renew under a stale fencing token is refused, and that the keeper stops issuing renewals once the lease is expired rather than resurrecting it.

A14. docs/operations/runner-local.md is updated to match the implementation, and only that document changes under docs/. It must state: the fake journey now carries a provider-neutral Work Packet and no prompt field exists; the journal recovery key is the increment identity so a different Execution can resume; the Secret Broker's two environment channels and its five fail-closed refusals; the bounded diagnostic log's caps and redaction; that OS-level workspace confinement is deferred; and that the Runner local durable store is the fsync-backed JSONL journal rather than SQLite, naming that as a recorded divergence from docs/architecture/technology.md section 10, not as a decision this task made.

A15. No file outside allowed_paths changes. In particular ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.json and devbox.lock are untouched, because internal/ci/planner.go evidenceKey() hashes ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.lock into every component's evidence key, so touching any of them invalidates all 23 component keys and every committed evidence record including the M0 and M1 gate evidence. test/journeys/ is not created: ValidateTracked requires exactly one owning component per tracked file, so it cannot exist without the prohibited ci/components.json edit and make ownership would fail. Nothing under internal/provider, internal/application, internal/store, internal/api or internal/domain non-test files changes.

A16. Exactly one evidence record, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-016-runner.json, is created with id ev-v2-016-runner, task_id V2-016 (the producer), component runner and result passed, holding one check per acceptance item above with the argv actually executed and its timeout. Its evidence_key is the runner component key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree at which devbox run --pure -- make check, format included, is green, because a formatting-only change moves the key. The record is registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of the record file's bytes, and devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts is green. That pair, registered in the index and the ledger test green, is the definition of done, not merely that the tests passed.

A17. After committing the evidence, devbox run --pure -- make check is green on the committed state, because gitleaks git scans committed history and never scans an uncommitted working tree. Checkpoints are pushed one at a time by the coordinator and the parent commit's v2 selective CI is confirmed green before the next push, per docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 10.

A18. No acceptance item is reported as passed unless its argv was actually executed in this task. No claim in this task substitutes for V2-017: the work report must state explicitly that a fake Invocation and a parsed fixture are not evidence about a real Codex CLI, and that the M3 completion condition 'Codex's real Preview capability succeeds' is untouched by this task and remains owned by V2-017 under G3.
constraints: Local closure only. Do not invoke codex, claude or opencode, do not start any real Provider CLI, do not consume Provider quota, and do not read any real credential from the environment, an OS keyring or disk. Every credential in every test is generated inside the test from crypto/rand and never leaves t.TempDir().

Determinism is an acceptance property, not a preference. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock dependence, no background timer, and no dependence on another test's execution order or residual processes. Synchronise only on an observable file or state with a bounded deadline and t.Fatal on timeout. If a test cannot be made deterministic, stop and escalate; do not quarantine it and do not retry it into a pass, because docs/architecture/validation.md section 9 forbids promoting a result that varied.

Do not create test/journeys/ and do not edit ci/components.json. If the work appears to require a new component, stop and escalate to product_orchestrator: ci/** is in all_on_change and ci/components.json is hashed into every component's evidence key, so the change invalidates the M0 and M1 gate evidence while two other implementers hold .agents/v2/evidence/** open.

internal/domain non-test files and contracts/schemas/** are prohibited. The M1 gate proved closure over exactly those files; reopening them is a cross-boundary redesign. If the resume path or the Secret Broker appears to need a new domain type, a new PermitKind or a schema field, stop and escalate with the exact type and the reason.

internal/provider is prohibited. Its public API (WorkPacket, Adapter, Invocation, Result, ClassifyError, DigestOutput, and the already-present Invocation.Environment) is sufficient. If a change there becomes unavoidable, stop and escalate: it would require a second evidence record whose component is owned by V2-027 at M6.

internal/application, internal/store/memory and internal/reconciler are prohibited. Claim already reclaims an expired lease with a fence bump, and Renew, Heartbeat, Checkpoint and AcceptResult already exist. If the journey needs a canonical change, stop and escalate rather than widening the blast radius.
Do not write any task-state file. Sol owns every .agents/v2/task-state transition and the coordinator edits that directory concurrently. Report the exact block_reason string instead.

.agents/v2/evidence/index.json is being edited concurrently. Add only the single ev-v2-016-runner entry, never rewrite or reorder another task's entry, and after any rebase recompute evidence_hash on the final bytes of the record file before declaring the ledger test green.

Escalate to product_orchestrator, do not decide alone: (1) whether adopting a pre-crash local provider checkpoint under a new, strictly greater fencing token is consistent with safety invariant 11, per dp-v2-016 d17 -- if it is not, journey 4 case B must always re-run the provider and A5 must be rewritten before implementation; (2) the SQLite versus fsync-JSONL divergence in docs/architecture/technology.md section 10 and docs/architecture/validation.md section 2, per dp-v2-016 d13; (3) the deferred move of journey tests to test/journeys/ and the batched ci/components.json dependency correction, per dp-v2-016 d2 and d16; (4) any demand that OS-enforced namespace confinement be proved at the M3 gate, per dp-v2-016 d12.

Escalate to tech_lead, do not guess: any acceptance item whose target boundary, observable or validation entry point is unclear, and any second consecutive failure of the same acceptance item. The retry budget for this task is 2 attempts.

Rollback is a single git revert of this task's checkpoint commits. No external state, no cloud resource and no credential is created, so nothing outside the repository needs undoing; the only side effects are files under the allowed paths.
Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree. Do not commit or push outside it; the coordinator pushes checkpoints one at a time and waits for the parent commit's CI.
Japanese for the tracked documents; English identifiers in code, schemas and configuration.
